Pedestrians use different things like umbrellas and small electric fans to cope with the intense heat while crossing the street in Cubao, Quezon City on April 25, 2024.
The STAR / Miguel de Guzman
MANILA, Philippines — Thirteen areas experienced danger-level heat index yesterday, according to the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration.
Masbate City, Borongan in Eastern Samar and Zamboanga City recorded 44 degrees Celsius.
Puerto Princesa City and Cuyo in Palawan recorded 43 degrees Celsius.

Areas that reported 42 degrees Celsius are Mulanay, Quezon; Coron, Palawan; Pili, Camarines Sur; Roxas City, Capiz; Iloilo City and Dumangas in Iloilo; La Granja in La Carlota City, Negros Occidental and Catarman, Northern Samar.
A danger-level heat index ranges from 42 to 51 degrees Celsius.
State meteorologists advised the public to drink plenty of water, avoid going outside between 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. and use sunscreen.
Meanwhile, cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms will be felt in Isabela and Aurora due to the easterlies.

articles.title: ‘Very clear’ evidence sought in VP trial
articles.summary: Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano hopes for clear evidence to help them decide whether to convict or acquit Vice President Sara Duterte, whose impeachment trial resumes today after a break…

blocks.text: November 19, 2026 | 12:00am
Alan Peter Cayetano and Sara Duterte
Ryan Baldemor / The Philippine STAR, Vice President Sara Duterte via Facebook

MANILA, Philippines — Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano hopes for clear evidence to help them decide whether to convict or acquit Vice President Sara Duterte, whose impeachment trial resumes today after a break due to the ASEAN Summit hosting.

“I’m hoping the evidence will be very, very clear to acquit or very, very clear to convict,” Cayetano said in a chance interview after attending the 51st National Prayer Breakfast at Club Filipino in San Juan.

A verdict not based on strong evidence would only “further divide the country” on such a polarizing topic, according to Cayetano, who pushed for addressing the country’s “political, spiritual and economic battle.”

Senate impeachment court spokesman Reginald Tongol said the defense team is expected to field four witnesses today and tomorrow to testify about CALE88 Foods Corp., a banana chips manufacturer, which prosecutors alleged had received a P319-million “remittance” from Chinese companies.

They are Rainer dela Fuente, who will testify about the Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLC); Ceferino Rodolfo, Department of Trade and Industry undersecretary, who will testify on CALE88’s registration with the Board of Investments; Pilar Marilyn Pagayunan of the Food and Drug Administration, who will testify on Cale88’s FDA product registration for its sweetened banana chips, and Rowena Mendoza from the DTI Center for International Trade Expositions and Missions, or her representative, about the communications and invitations sent to CALE88 for food expositions.
“All four are covered by requests for Subpoena Ad Testificandum and Duces Tecum to controvert allegations under Article II,” Tongol said.

When the prosecution presented its AMLC witness, executive director Ronel Buenaventura last month, senators tackled the possibility that CALE88 may have been used for money laundering after it allegedly received funds from China.
The Vice President’s husband Manases Carpio holds a 47.5 percent share in CALE88.
Duterte may be convicted by the court as some senators are reportedly being “pressured,” Duterte’s spokesman Paolo Panelo claimed.
Honest mistake?

The House prosecution panel did not give any weight to the claim of the Vice President that she made an “honest mistake” when she declared GenCorp. Industries as one of her business interests in her statement of assets, liabilities and net worth (SALN).

House prosecutor Manila Rep. Joel Chua and prosecution team adviser Ace Barbers pointed out that Duterte repeatedly listed the company and its predecessors in her SALN, specifically for two consecutive years. — Evelyn Macairan, Daphne Galvez

articles.title: DepEd’s AI tool to catch early learning deficiencies
articles.summary: Within 15 minutes, the newly developed artificial intelligence tool of the Department of Education can assess learners who are at risk of learning and communication difficulties.

blocks.text: November 19, 2026 | 12:00am

In a statement yesterday, Education Secretary Sonny Angara said that through their Project SABAY or Screening using AI-Based Assistance for Young Children, they would be able to screen Grade 2 learners for risks of learning and communication difficulties, which is an improvement over traditional methods that can take up to two hours per learner.

MANILA, Philippines — Within 15 minutes, the newly developed artificial intelligence (AI) tool of the Department of Education (DepEd) can assess learners who are at risk of learning and communication difficulties.
He said the AI-based tool is meant to empower educators and give parents clear insights to support their child’s development.

“By providing them with transparent, data-driven tools that show step-by-step results, we are giving our teachers the confidence and clarity they need to partner effectively with parents and secure early interventions,” he said.

The AI app was developed by the Bureau of Learning Delivery and the Education Center for AI Research. It transforms the typically tedious screening process into an engaging, story-driven experience that makes young children feel comfortable and stress-free.

Through a teacher-assisted application, learners complete gamified speech tasks such as picture naming, word dictation, nonsense word dictation and spontaneous vocalization. Its interactive format makes screening more natural and less stressful for young learners.

School heads and teachers have also praised the platform’s transparency, noting that its step-by-step analytical breakdown helps them clearly explain screening results to parents and build stronger partnerships for learner intervention.
The system also addresses a critical bottleneck in the country’s health care and educational support network.

After its initial pilot testing in the National Capital Region, DepEd has expanded data collection across the Visayas, Mindanao and upcoming regions in Luzon to ensure the AI tool adapts effectively to the country’s diverse cultural and linguistic landscape.
P440 million sought for more counselors

The Second Congressional Commission on Education (EDCOM 2) yesterday advocated for an additional allocation of P440 million for 1,100 school counselor associate positions in the national budget for 2027, on top of the 3,000 SCA positions included in the proposed budget.

EDCOM 2 cited the 2022 Program for International Student Assessment data where 43 percent of Filipino girls and 53 percent of boys were reported being bullied a few times a month, with rates roughly twice the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development average.

The 2024 Southeast Asia Primary Learning Metrics also discovered that 50 percent of Filipino Grade 5 learners experienced bullying at least once a month, which is reportedly the highest rate in Southeast Asia.

articles.title: VP Sara’s camp: House discussing no-el in 2028
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte’s spokesman Paolo Panelo said yesterday that he had received confirmation about ongoing discussions at the House of Representatives about a no-elections scenario in…

blocks.text: November 19, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte’s spokesman Paolo Panelo said yesterday that he had received confirmation about ongoing discussions at the House of Representatives about a no-elections (no-el) scenario in 2028.
In an interview over Bilyonaryo News Channel, Panelo said there are talks at the House of Representatives about “no-el” in 2028.

Panelo said in one of their recent conversations, he asked the Vice President what would happen in case she is convicted by the Senate impeachment court and be disqualified to run in the 2028 national elections.
Panelo asked Duterte who would take her place as presidential candidate.

“Her only reply to me was, ‘Oh, attorney, we don’t even know if we would reach the 2028 elections because the information I have been receiving is there is a plan for a ‘no-el’ in 2028, whether that’s by term extensions or converting our form of government into parliamentary,’” said Panelo.
“Since there have been such rumors, and after talking to her, I have received confirmation that there are talks in the Lower House about this,” he added.
Election lawyer Romulo Macalintal has warned that the law postponing this year’s barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan elections could inspire the postponement as well of the 2028 general elections.

Commission on Elections (Comelec) Chairman George Garcia earlier dismissed the possibility of “no-election” in 2028, adding that the poll body has already been preparing for the upcoming national elections.
Former VP helpers ‘safe and sound’
Meanwhile, Panelo said with the help of the police, two former members of the Vice President’s household staff have been found, released and are safe.

Panelo said that on Tuesday, “the Vice President, through her legal team and with the assistance of the police, has since facilitated the release of two former household staff members. They are now safe and sound.”
Duterte’s legal team, accompanied by police officers, reportedly fetched them and brought them to a police station where they executed affidavits. The incident was recorded in the police blotter.
“For now, the apparent plan to use these individuals for false testimony against the Vice President has been foiled,” Panelo said.
Earlier, he raised suspicion that the alleged threats made against the two household staff members could be linked to the Marcos administration.
Panelo said they sought the help of the Philippine National Police (PNP) after one of the household helpers reached out to the Vice President and sought her help, asking that they be rescued.

The helpers said that sometime in October, they were recruited by a private individual to work as employees at a resort in Boracay. They were brought to Manila under the pretext of training for the job.
On Nov. 16, their employer reportedly informed them that there were threats to their lives, and that there was also a threat to the employer’s own life because he was reportedly “harboring” them.

“The employer then told them that the threats would be quelled if they executed affidavits, drafts of which were presented to them. According to the two individuals, the affidavits contained false allegations against the Vice President, which they refused to sign,” Panelo said.
This prompted them to seek the help of the Vice President.
“It was later clarified that they were not held in captivity, but they were afraid to leave the employer’s custody due to the supposed threat to their lives,” Panelo said.

articles.title: Marcos thanks Pinoys for patience during ASEAN meet
articles.summary: President Marcos thanked the Filipino people for their “patience, understanding and cooperation” during the country’s hosting of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations Summit…

blocks.text: November 19, 2026 | 12:00am
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. speaks during a press briefing at the International Media Center in Pasay City on November 17, 2026)
Ryan Baldemor / The Philippine STAR

MANILA, Philippines — President Marcos thanked the Filipino people for their “patience, understanding and cooperation” during the country’s hosting of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit and related summits this year.?

“I also wish to express my special thanks to the Filipino people, particularly those whose daily routines were affected by the preparations and activities surrounding the summit,” Marcos said on Tuesday.?
“For that warmth and generosity you have shown our guests, you have once again demonstrated the hospitality for which Filipinos are known around the world,” the President said.?

The Chief Executive likewise expressed his gratitude to government agencies, personnel and volunteers for their contribution to the country’s successful hosting of the bi-annual meeting of the 11-member regional bloc.?
“This was the product of the hard work and dedication of a multitude of people and agencies, each of whom played an important role in making this summit a success,” Marcos said.?
On Tuesday, the Philippines formally turned over the chairship of ASEAN to Singapore during the culmination of the summit at the Philippine International Convention Center in Pasay City.
Senators lauded the hosting of the ASEAN Summit even as the President’s sister, Sen. Imee Marcos, questioned the “prudence and proportionality” of the reported P22.9-billion cost for the chairship.
Sen. Erwin Tulfo questioned his colleague’s assessment of the ASEAN Summit based on its costs, as he pushed for evaluating the summit on “outcomes and commitments that will benefit our country soon.”

Reacting to the hundreds arrested for protesting Trump’s visit and the US-led artificial intelligence supply chain initiative Pax Silica, Sen. Panfilo Lacson cited his experience as former national police chief in believing authorities have intelligence to “handle the protests.”
Speaker Faustino Dy III urged lawmakers from Southeast Asian nations to work on legislation meant to increase trade and other avenues of cooperation as a bid to strengthen regional unity.
Meanwhile, the Department of Health said two very important delegates required medical assistance during the ASEAN Summit. — Marc Jayson Cayabyab, Rhodina Villanueva, Daphne Galvez

articles.title: Online scams a national security matter – ASEAN, US
articles.summary: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations and the United States urged governments to recognize online scams as a security matter that needs public-private partnership to combat the transnational…

blocks.text: November 19, 2026 | 12:00am
Stock image of an attempted scam.
Pixabay / File

MANILA, Philippines — The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and the United States urged governments to recognize online scams as a security matter that needs public-private partnership to combat the transnational organized criminal networks that may be behind the illegal activity.

On Tuesday, leaders of the ASEAN and the US adopted the Statement on 10 Public-Private Partnership Principles for Tackling Online Scams, which highlights shared interest in combating online scams, placing the disruption of criminal networks and the protection of victims as priorities.

“Public-private collaboration can be at its most efficient when it leverages existing frameworks to ensure that online scams, and the trafficking in persons that fuels them, are addressed at the highest levels of policymaking,” the statement read.

“Any public-private collaboration would aim to enhance safeguards to protect users from scams consistent with domestic law, raise awareness and facilitate information sharing to dismantle online scam compounds, [therefore] addressing human trafficking tied to forced criminality and disrupting illicit financial activity,” it noted.

articles.title: Lower airfares seen
articles.summary: Filipinos planning a trip for the Christmas holiday will get a slight relief in airfares, as the Civil Aeronautics Board has lowered the fuel surcharge by a notch until end-November.

blocks.text: November 19, 2026 | 12:00am
Stock photo of individuals waiting for their flight.
Unsplash / Filipe C. Sousa

MANILA, Philippines — Filipinos planning a trip for the Christmas holiday will get a slight relief in airfares, as the Civil Aeronautics Board (CAB) has lowered the fuel surcharge by a notch until end-November.
In an advisory, CAB said it is cutting the fuel surcharge to Level 16 for Nov. 16 to 30, from Level 17 formerly.
At Level 16, airlines can impose a fuel surcharge of P525 to P1,535 for domestic flights and a pass-on fee of P1,733.76 to P12,891.29 for international trips.
Filipinos headed for Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand have to pay P2,397.82 more under Level 16 while those headed to Indonesia, Japan and South Korea will have pay a fuel surcharge of P2,697.07.
The highest fuel surcharge will be slapped on travelers taking transpacific trips, hitting P7,530.97 for flights to Honolulu and P12,277.42 for departures to North America.
Locally, the highest fuel surcharge will be felt on Manila flights to General Santos at P1,535.
Manila trips to Cotabato, Davao and Zamboanga are accorded the second highest fuel surcharge among domestic destinations at P1,431.

CAB said airlines wishing to collect the fuel surcharge must submit an application to the agency. It also asked carriers transacting in foreign currencies to observe an exchange rate of P63.61 to $1 in collecting their fuel surcharge.
Based on the monitor of the International Air Transport Association, jet fuel prices have dropped by 12 percent on a monthly basis to $169.82 per barrel as of Sept. 18.
However, prices will continue to fluctuate due to the Middle East conflict.
For Filipinos, the slight reduction in fares opens a window for them to book flights, as they also deal with a weak peso that has made it costlier to travel internationally.
Historically, November marks the peak of the booking season for air travel, as Filipinos plan the trips that they would make on the Christmas and New Year holidays.

articles.title: Carpio: Political dynasties feed on national budget
articles.summary: Political dynasties have been “feeding on the budget” passed by Congress every year, and there is a need to remove them, according to retired Supreme Court senior associate justice…

blocks.text: Headlines
November 19, 2026 | 12:00am
Retired Supreme Court justice Antonio Carpio warned.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — Political dynasties have been “feeding on the budget” passed by Congress every year, and there is a need to remove them, according to retired Supreme Court senior associate justice Antonio Carpio.

Between 75 and 85 percent of the current members of the Senate and the House of Representatives belong to political dynasties, Carpio said. He noted that the number has ballooned since the ratification of the 1987 Constitution.

“That used to be 20 percent in 1987. How come they have grown so huge? They have intensified their control,” he said during an interview in a YouTube podcast hosted by content creator Carlo Ople on Tuesday.

Carpio said the people can fight back against political dynasties by joining an online campaign aimed at collecting signatures to be able to enact an anti-political dynasty law without approval from Congress.

With Congress enacting the General Appropriations Act (GAA) or the national budget every year, Carpio stressed that members of political dynasties in the two chambers are able to insert fund allocations or pork barrel, including the Priority Development Assistance Fund (PDAF) that has been declared unconstitutional.

This time, members of political dynasties in Congress make way for fund allocations by allotting them to flood control projects for instance, wherein 70 percent of the funds are “wasted,” he noted.?Caprio cited testimonies by former Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) undersecretary Roberto Bernardo that up to 25 percent of funds of flood control projects went to some lawmakers as kickbacks.

“How did the political dynasties grow? How did they come to dominate everything? Because of the money in the budget. Every year, they use that to buy votes. Therefore, the political dynasties feed on the budget every year… to perpetuate themselves and to enlarge themselves in power,” he said.

As political dynasties remain prevalent, coupled with high inflation rate currently at 7.8 percent and weak confidence of investors in the country due to corruption issues, Carpio warned the public might get fed up and launch a revolution similar to the riots in France and Italy since last month.
“It won’t take long and it will happen to us. So we have to prepare for that because if we have rioting, everybody suffers,” he warned.

Carpio is currently one of the convenors of the Dapat Isa Lang Movement, which would gather signatures of registered voters from three percent of each of the country’s 254 legislative districts or 10 percent of registered voters nationwide.

The proposed law would require that only one member of the family up to the fourth degree of relationship, also applicable to spouses and his or her family members, will seek each national and local elective public office.
It could be passed into law through a people’s initiative, without relying on the approval of Congress, according to Carpio.

Meanwhile, Caloocan Rep. Edgar Erice urged the Senate to look at congressional insertions in the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027 as red flags which deserve further scrutiny. — Daphne Galvez

MANILA, Philippines — United States President Donald Trump praised President Marcos’ “very good genetics” and called his son, House Majority Leader Sandro Marcos, “a beautiful young man.”
In his speech during the Association of Southeast Asian Nations-US Special Summit Tuesday night, Trump thanked Marcos for “a beautiful welcome” as he returned to the country.

“I just don’t want to date myself, but I knew your parents very well and they were great. I believe in genetics and they did a good job. You have very good genetics, I can tell you that,” the US leader said.

“Your family is amazing. You’re amazing. And I just met your son. He’s a beautiful young man. He’s got a great future. And it’s an honor to meet you, especially to meet you, OK? You’ve done a good job. Your parents have done a very good job. So, it’s a great honor,” he added.
The Ilocos Norte representative was among the officials who welcomed Trump during his arrival in Manila Tuesday afternoon. Trump was seen talking to Sandro at the airport.

A social media post yesterday also showed Trump exchanging pleasantries with Marcos’ mother, former first lady Imelda Marcos, before his departure for Shenzhen, China for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Summit.
“We love you,” Trump told Marcos as she greeted him.
During their bilateral meeting at Malacañang yesterday, Marcos revealed having asked his staff on Tuesday to deliver food from Jollibee to Trump and his delegation “as a late night snack.”
“However, since you’re strapped for time, I thought the taste of Manila might be, might be good,” Marcos said.

“I think they gave you the… Jollibee is a very, very popular chain. And one of their main products is fried chicken, and we are very proud to say that we have surpassed KFC in the United States in terms of popularity,” Marcos said, to which the US leader responded, “Oh, wow. Fantastic.”

Trump also praised Marcos’ “excellent leadership” as chair of the ASEAN this year. Trump told ASEAN leaders the US is “deeply committed to the success, sovereignty and prosperity of our many friends and partners.”
‘Call me’

Also during the ASEAN-US Summit, Trump promised to be always accessible to Southeast Asian leaders and joked that he would immediately fire Secretary of State Marco Rubio if he failed to respond quickly to their concerns.
He reiterated his support for allies in what he called “one of the world’s most vibrant and productive regions.”
He also called ASEAN countries “great friends” of the US.
In his speech, Trump said Washington is “deeply committed” to the success, sovereignty and prosperity of its friends and partners. “We’re with you always,” he said.

“We support our partners and our allies 100 percent. And when there’s a problem, you call me. You’ll call (US State Secretary) Marco (Rubio). You’ll call others. And if they don’t respond, call me. I’ll take your call. I’ll say, ‘Marco, you’re fired. You didn’t, you didn’t respond fast enough,’” he added.

articles.title: TV buyer's guide for the holidays: OLED, micro RGB, QNED, LCD?!
articles.summary: Buying a TV used to be very straightforward. In the past, knowing how far your couch was from the television mount was enough information to determine how many screen inches your TV should be. In…

blocks.text: Buying a TV used to be very straightforward. In the past, knowing how far your couch was from the television mount was enough information to determine how many screen inches your TV should be. In these modern times, that is no longer the case. The LCD panel of yore has evolved into its different iterations – from LED, OLED, micro RGB, to having different types of finishes (such as matte!), to resolutions like 4K and 8K, and AI assistant functions. The living room TV has evolved from being just a living room entertainment hub, into a full blown home command center.

blocks.caption: LG event

blocks.text: This is a guide to help dispel and educate what kind of TV you should be buying for your living room.

It is important to note that different brands use a lot of marketing jargon. While consumer electronics marketing often relies on proprietary branding, the premium market fundamentally divides into three primary display philosophies: Self-Emissive Displays (OLED) , Dedicated Primary Color Micro Emitters (Micro RGB / Mini RGB) , and Quantum-Enhanced Backlit LCDs (QNED / Mini-LED). At the recent holiday event from LG Electronics, they showcased different use cases for each type.
Choosing a display

Every consumer television creates an image through the precise interplay of illumination and chrominance. However, the mechanical method by which light is generated and manipulated dictates things like black levels, color saturation, off-axis viewing stability, and peak luminance.
Why choose OLED

Self-emissive Organic Light-Emitting Diode (OLED) technology functions without an external backlight unit. In an OLED panel, every individual sub-pixel produces its own light and color, allowing each pixel to be dimmed or completely turned off independently of its neighbors.

Because inactive pixels produce zero light output, self-emissive displays deliver true black levels and infinite native contrast. In scenes featuring high dynamic contrast—such as bright city lights against a midnight sky or starfields in deep space—there is no light bleeding or haloing (“blooming”) into surrounding dark areas. This pixel-level control provides an image that remains the reference standard for color grading suites and film directors.

This simply means that OLED technology is best for true cinephiles who want to enjoy a film the way a director intended it. Blooming effects can get out of hand especially with white subtitles, and for people with astigmatism. Sometimes when viewing YouTube videos or playing certain video games, you can never get a true “black” screen in horror films or scenes that portray dark areas unless you are watching on an OLED display.
Why choose Micro RGB and Mini RGB

Micro RGB and Mini RGB architectures represent a major advancement in solid-state lighting and color science. Rather than utilizing standard blue LEDs coated with yellow phosphor or shining a broad-spectrum white backlight through subtractive color filters, Micro RGB displays employ microscopic, dedicated primary red, green, and blue light sources.

By generating primary light directly at the emitter stage, Micro RGB technology achieves an extraordinary degree of spectral accuracy. In traditional filtered LCDs or standard phosphor-driven panels, driving high peak brightness can wash out delicate hues, causing deep crimsons, emerald greens, and rich cyans to shift toward white. Micro RGB eliminates this color clipping, maintaining full chromatic saturation and spectral purity across the entire brightness curve.

blocks.caption: micro RGB from LG

blocks.text: Micro RGB is best for people who like to use their TV as an art centerpiece. There have been times when photos displayed on Micro RGB are mistaken to be mounted photos — because the colors look and feel that way. Micro RGB is also great for gamers that want to experience a wide gamut of crisp colors when they play. A high refresh rate screen usually accompanies this, such as the C6 series.
Why choose QNED and Mini-LED

Quantum Nano-Emitting Diode (QNED) and Mini-LED displays represent the pinnacle of liquid crystal display (LCD) engineering. Unlike legacy direct-lit or edge-lit screens that rely on dozens of large LED modules, Mini-LED backlights employ thousands of miniaturized LED chips arranged in an ultra-dense array behind the LCD panel, controlled across hundreds or thousands of independent local dimming zones.

blocks.caption: QNED TV

blocks.text: QNED technology is great for studios and family rooms that let in a lot of light. Imagine a studio that has a strong key light shining directly at the host with a TV in the background. A regular TV would have a lot of glare. QNED technology removes that hassle to make the viewing experience better.
AI on remote

One of the eye-catching fascinations of the new generation of LG evo AI TV’s is the AI Magic Remote that automatically customizes according to the user’s voice. That would mean having different profiles at home depending on who is using the remote control without having to switch users.

This is a basic guide to the different screen technologies available in the market today. Consumers can mix and match features depending on budget and needs because these days, there’s a TV for everyone!

articles.title: Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries as first Black House speaker despite progressives’ concerns
articles.summary: Jeffries is set to become one of Trump’s most prominent opponents for final two years of his presidency

blocks.text: Democrats on Wednesday nominated Hakeem Jeffries to serve as speaker of the House when the new Congress begins next year.

A New York congressman who has served as the Democratic minority leader since 2023, Jeffries is set to become one of Donald Trump’s most prominent opponents for the final two years of his presidency, when Democrats will control both the Senate and House of Representatives and undertake aggressive efforts to check his powers.

Jeffries was nominated despite concerns from some progressives that he represents a politically risky status quo for a party that is looking to capitalize on a surprisingly good performance in the midterms, where voters swept them back into power in both the House and Senate with significant majorities.

Jeffries is set to be formally elected speaker when the House of Representatives convenes at the beginning of next year, with Democrats controlling a majority of at least 257 seats, their largest in nearly two decades. The 56-year-old would become the first Black lawmaker to serve as House speaker, and the first Democrat since Nancy Pelosi, who is set to retire from Congress at the end of this year.

No other Democrat stood against Jeffries for the job, and his party nominated him by a recorded vote at their behind-closed-doors caucus meeting. They also selected California congressman Ted Lieu to serve as caucus chair.

In office since 2013, Jeffries was House Democratic caucus chair when Pelosi served as speaker from 2019 to 2023. He took over as leader when she stepped down after Democrats lost their House majority in 2022, but rankled progressives by refusing to endorse proposals to create a Medicare for All healthcare system, and for not taking a strong stance against aid to Israel amid accusations it carried out a genocide in Gaza. Earlier this month, Indivisible, a nationwide progressive organizing group, released a poll that found only 28% of registered voters view Jeffries favorably.

He’s recently sought to bridge those divides, and on Tuesday announced his support for lowering the age of eligibility for Medicare, and expanding its coverage to include vision and dental treatments, and to offer it to children. He’s also called for “dramatic change” in the US relationship with Israel, though in July did not vote for an amendment that would have cut military aid to the Middle Eastern ally.

In the run-up to the vote, Don Leonard, a newly elected Democrat representing an Ohio district Donald Trump won in the 2024 election, told CNN he wouldn’t vote for Jeffries unless he won commitments to end aid to Israel, and undo the supreme court’s Citizens United ruling, which allowed outside groups to spend unlimited amounts on elections.
Shortly before the vote, he confirmed to the network that because Jeffries had not met his demands, he wouldn’t vote for him.

articles.title: Who speaks for Europe abroad? Not its top diplomat
articles.summary: EU leaders’ decision to exclude the bloc’s foreign policy chief from their negotiating lineup for Russia peace talks reveals how national turf wars undermine Brussels’ global…

blocks.text: The EU, we are repeatedly told, wants (and needs) to be a global player, a geopolitical heavyweight capable of shaping its own foreign and security policies – or at the very least, speaking with one clear, unambiguous voice on the world stage.

Last Friday’s summit in Dublin, when leaders debated who should represent the bloc in talks aimed at ending Russia’s war on Ukraine – the gravest security crisis the EU has faced in decades – showed once again that it is unlikely to find such a voice anytime soon.

The EU has a chief diplomat: she is called Kaja Kallas, she is a former Estonian prime minister, and she was appointed the EU’s High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy, and a European Commission vice-president, in 2024.

In theory, Kallas should embody this more assertive Europe. But as the US-mediated talks accelerate, EU leaders have – despite Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s pleas for the bloc to field a single negotiator – locked her out of the room.

Instead, alongside US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, Europe is being represented by a seven-strong team: European Council president António Costa, Commission president Ursula von der Leyen, and representatives from the E5 powers: France, Germany, Britain, Poland, and Italy, working with Nato.

On paper, Kallas’s job description is straightforward and twofold. She chairs the Foreign Affairs Council, the monthly decision-making forum where national foreign ministers meet to agree on common EU foreign policy, sanctions and crisis responses.

She also runs the European External Action Service (EEAS), the bloc’s permanent diplomatic corps and de facto foreign ministry, made up of civil servants and over 140 embassies around the world that carry out day-to-day EU diplomacy on the ground.

In practice, being the face of EU foreign policy – a role created by the Lisbon Treaty in 2009 to answer Henry Kissinger’s famous if apocryphal question “Who do I call when I want to talk to Europe?” – is, as one commentator puts it, a “poisoned chalice”.

Jennifer Rankin in Brussels tells me: “Personally, I think Kallas has an impossible job: having to represent the positions of 27 member states that often disagree on foreign policy, and don’t want to cede real decision making on it to the EU.”

Relations between Kallas and von der Leyen – who critics accuse of sharing exactly the same kind of power-hoarding and centralising instincts as some EU national leaders – have been particularly difficult.

That friction has been aggravated by active proposals in Brussels to overhaul the bloc’s whole diplomatic service, folding parts of the EEAS and key foreign policy powers directly into the Commission president’s remit.

On Friday, when the Dublin summit convened, Kallas was unequivocal: leaders had agreed in 2024, when it was clear there would have to be talks with Russia, “that I’mthe one who is representing Europe in foreign and security policy,” she said.
But when Costa announced the bloc’s negotiators in Dublin, Kallas wasn’t among them. So why did the 27 capitals bypass the person they hired for the job?
Three explanations are doing the diplomatic rounds. First, several western European capitals view the Estonian envoy as too overtly, and fiercely, anti-Russian.

Second, there is a much deeper reflex at play: the EU’s big member states simply refuse to cede real foreign policy power to Brussels. Paris and Berlin in particular resist a single EU envoy, clearly preferring to protect their own seats at the table.
Third, diplomats point to a wider trend for the kind of international questions once handled by foreign ministers being taken over by premiers or presidents.

Whatever the reason, von der Leyen’s defence of the decision was brisk: “We decide for ourselves who will represent us, and we made that decision today,” she said. Germany’s chancellor, Friedrich Merz, has also argued that intergovernmental formats like the E3 – France, Germany and the UK – are “a well-established format” and “I see absolutely no problem with keeping it that way.”

Others, though, were less happy. Spain and Lithuania both criticised the team approach. “Europe needs one voice,” said Lithuania’s foreign minister, Kęstutis Budrys. “We cannot speak with 27 microphones. We need one.”
A damaging own goal?
after newsletter promotion

blocks.caption: Kaja Kallas is supposed to be the face of EU foreign policy. Photograph: Cathal McNaughton/Reuters

blocks.text: All this may seem rather inside-the-Brussels-beltway stuff. But beneath it lies a real, and important debate over whether the EU will ever be a global actor, or be fated to remain a disjointed collection of national voices.

Defenders of the Dublin decision argue that hard security and ending the war are issues that belong to the EU’s major military and financial powers, not supranational officials: bringing the big beasts to the table provides the real geopolitical heft.

One EU diplomat said the problem was that EU institutions “do not have sufficient political legitimacy in the eyes of voters. And this matters big time. The E5 solution is an attempt to bridge that gap.”
But critics see a damaging own goal, and a profound hypocrisy. Brussels commenter Dave Keating argues there is a fatal contradiction inherent in Europe’s integration.

Member states “know what the right thing to do is in the abstract, so they create these positions and institutions to make a stronger EU,” he says. “But then … they undermine [them] … because they always give in to the urge not to hand over power to someone else.”

By choosing to field what Keating called a “European cacophony” that would inevitably be dismissed as irrelevant by Moscow and Washington, leaders proved Kallas’s job “is not real, and the EU doesn’t actually have a foreign policy”, he said.

Jennifer is slightly less damning. “I think the E5+ format could be seen as a realistic answer to represent the EU as it is, not the idealised union of the treaties,” she said. “It needn’t be a cacophony if everyone in the room has the same message.”
So far, on Ukraine at least, there is a large degree of consensus. But if, for example, Marine Le Pen becomes French president, all bets are off,” says Jennifer.

For her part, Kallas has put a brave face on it, insisting she will focus on “substance” while leaders handle “format”. But the suspicion remains: Europe’s leaders want the bloc to be a global power, but won’t let anyone else speak for them.
Until they do, the risk is that the EU will be stuck on the diplomatic sidelines, forever punching below its geopolitical weight.

articles.title: Parents jailed for torture and death of four-year-old girl in France in 1987
articles.summary: Inass Touloub's body was found along the A10 road in 1987, bearing marks of abuse, and was not identified until 2018.

blocks.text: The mother of a four-year-old girl killed in central France and found along a motorway almost 40 years ago has been sentenced to 20 years in prison.
Halima El Bakhti, 72, was found guilty on Tuesday of "torture and acts of barbarity resulting in death without the intent to kill", French media reports.
The girl's father, 74-year-old Ahmed Touloub, was handed a 15-year sentence as an accomplice.

Four-year-old Inass Touloub was found along the A10 road in Suèvres in the Loir-et-Cher department on 11 August 1987. Her body bore multiple marks of abuse, including human bite marks, broken bones and burns with an iron.
She was buried in an unmarked grave near the location where her body was found. Unidentified for three decades, she was known only as the "Little Martyr of the A10".
Then, in 2018, she was identified after the DNA of her brother – tested in an unrelated case – matched with hers, leading to the arrest of their parents.
The trial took place in Loir-et-Cher Assize Court from 2 November, with the verdict delivered on Tuesday after several hours of deliberation.

During the trial, prosecutor Anaïs Allio emphasised that "not a single part of Inass's body was spared", and recalled the "sense of vertigo that overcame us all" upon viewing the "unbearable photographs" from the autopsy, France Info reports.
The jury concluded that the child's mother was suffering from impaired judgement at the time of the girl's death, which reduced the maximum potential sentence.
French media outlet France Info described the two defendants as sitting stoically in chairs before the court with their heads bowed as the reasoning behind the verdict was read out.
El Bakhti and Touloub have 10 days to appeal the verdict.
Inass's death sparked one of France's biggest ever investigations, with the girl's photograph posted in public places and an alert sent to more than 30 countries.

articles.title: Borussia Dortmund bows to fan pressure and end Rheinmetall deal
articles.summary: Borussia Dortmund has reluctantly ended its association with a major sponsor after long-term fan protests. They are not the first Bundesliga club to u-turn, as commercial interests clash with…

image.caption: Borussia Dortmund fans have long objected to the club's links with RheinmetallImage: Bernd Thissen/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Two years of fan pressure and criticism has forced Borussia Dortmund to drop a sponsorship deal with Germany's largest arms manufacturer, Rheinmetall.

The Bundesliga club will not renew its deal with Rheinmetall beyond its expiry in June 2027, at the end of this season. Dortmund chairman Carsten Cramer confirmed the news on the club's website ahead of its AGM on Sunday, which may have proved a potential flashpoint. He acknowledged that "our partnership has been controversial from the outset" but lamented the loss of income.
"It reduces our financial room for manoeuvre. We will have to reprioritize planned investments and carefully examine how we can find viable solutions."
Though he welcomed the news, one of the leaders of the fan revolt against the partnership, Michael Schulze von Glaser, warned this is likely not the end of the road.
Germans protest Rheinmetall's plans for Berlin arms factory

"I think in the end it was a victory for the fans. But I'm also a bit skeptical about what the future will bring us," the Dortmund fan and former head of the German Peace Society told DW. "Football fans in Germany always must be skeptical and always must watch what the club is doing.”
Long held opposition

Many Dortmund fans have opposed the deal — which has seen Rheinmetall's logo on advertising boards and other surfaces at locations such as Dortmund's 83,000-capacity Westfalenstadion — from its beginnings in 2024. It was estimated to be worth between €7 ($7.68 million) and €9 million per year.

At the club's AGM that year, 556 of 855 members present voted against the deal in a non-binding vote. There were 247 votes in favour, with 52 abstentions. This, said Cramer, informed the eventual outcome.

Rheinmetall sells arms mostly to Germany, Ukraine and NATO but fans and critics feel that platforming any arms manufacturer goes against the club's statement of its core values. In that, Dortmund states its desire for "a club and a society that operate free of racism, anti-Semitism, LGBTQIA+ hostility, sexism, violence and discrimination."

It has always been clear, said Schulze von Glaser, that this deal did not chime with that.

"In the end, they kill people. They are for war," he said of Rheinmetall. "The slogan of Borussia Dortmund is true love (Echte Liebe). But for me and many others, our love ends there…. I know some fans who have put fan merchandise in the trash because they were so shocked.”

In the Q and A on the club's website, Cramer said he was still a "personal advocate" of the deal but that Dortmund's commitment to the 50+1 model, which means German clubs are majority controlled by the members, meant they had to listen to fan voices. But he also warned that Rheinmetall must be an "absolute exception and an isolated case."
That set off some alarm bells for Schulze von Glaser.
"It's a bit concerning that there are constantly these attacks on professional football — a new sponsorship, investment deals," he said.
Dortmund not the first to climbdown on sponsors

Indeed, Dortmund's climbdown is not the first of its kind in Germany's top flight. Last year, after fan and media pressure, Bayern Munich ended its commercial deal with the tourism arm of the Rwandan government before its conclusion.

Fans had objected to the promotion of Rwanda, which many felt sought to divert attention from its poor human rights record and actions in the war with DR Congo, through sporting partnerships. Two years earlier, Bayern withdrew from a similarly controversial deal with Qatar Airways.

blocks.caption: Both Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund have rethought sponsorship deals of lateImage: Alexandra Beier/AFP

blocks.text: Elsewhere in the league, Werder Bremen fans objected to their long time shirt sponsor, Wiesenhof. Many supporters took issue with the factory farming practices of Germany's largest poultry producer. Though it was not given as a direct reason for the end of a shirt sponsorship deal in 2023, it likely played a part.

Union Berlin fans have also made their voices heard. When the club signed a new shirt-sponsorship deal with Luxembourg real estate company, Aroundtown, upon promotion to the top flight in 2019, many fans were frustrated at the tie up in a city where rent prices were skyrocketing.
German football's battle between commerce and 50+1
"It's a problem for a lot of people," fan Sven Dobberstein told DW at the time.
"We have to try to find a way between commercialization and what we have at the moment. It isn't easy."

Striking that balance can often be a source of tension for Bundesliga clubs. 50+1 ensures fans have a voice, preventing rich owners, or nation states, from taking control as they do in England's lucrative Premier League or in France or Spain. Indeed fan protests have also stopped the league signing a €1billion private equity partner and seen Monday night matches scrapped. For Schulze von Glaser, this needs to be protected.
"In Germany, the fan culture has an impact," he said.

”If there is something bad or terrible happening in your club and in the Bundesliga, there are the organized fans and they can have an impact if they want, if they stand together and, yes, they can stop the Rheinmetall deal."
Additional reporting by: Emmie Eernisse

articles.title: EXPLAINER: Why is the Trump administration pushing for Pax Silica?
articles.summary: In the days leading up to US President Donald Trump"s visit to the Philippines, protesters have rallied against him and the planned Pax Silica initiative -- but why has his administration kept…

blocks.text: In the days leading up to US President Donald Trump’s visit to the Philippines, protesters have rallied against him and the planned Pax Silica initiative — but why has his administration kept pushing for the project?
In a report from GMA News Feed, the Pax Silica project is a flagship effort of the US to strengthen AI ecosystems.
According to the US Department of State, the Pax Silica project wants to secure the supply chain for creating a Super Intelligence (SI) by developing an “economic consensus” among allies,
Included in the supply chain are the materials and resources needed for AI, including critical minerals, energy, manufacturing, semiconductors, and other infrastructure like data centers.

The US think tank Council on Foreign Relations believes that the Pax Silica project is an attempt to get resources to develop advanced AI technology. Others believe that the US wants to maintain its superiority in AI development.

“US still considers itself as retaining superiority in terms of the development of these AI tools and software. However, there are serious concerns by the US, on the fact that China can acquire technology and know-how to develop their own and quickly catch up, so essentially gaining an edge in the AI race,” said UP Department of Political Science Senior Lecturer Matteo Piasentini.
Piasentini said that the US was using Pax Silica as “tactical practice” to show its dominance to China. The US was also making use of the Philippines for cheap labor to manufacture AI parts.

“To use a metaphor, it’s great powers waving shiny objects in the international system, and creating incentives for, let's say, smaller states to explore, right? Possibilities, opportunities, while, you know, putting question marks against, on the other part, on the counterpart or the other power that used to or that thought would retain dominance over certain sectors of the economy,” he said.

According to the US-based Center for Strategic and International Studies, the US and China saw Southeast Asia as an area of competition. Among ASEAN members, the Philippines and Singapore signed the Pax Silica initiative.

Meanwhile, seven countries from Southeast Asia, namely Malaysia, Indonesia, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Viet Nam and Brunei, are part of the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization --- an AI initiative by China. However, other parts of Southeast Asia are unlikely to choose sides.

“I don't think anyone in the United States is naive enough to think that Southeast Asian countries will choose between Pax Silica and the Chinese initiative. Southeast Asian countries, apart from the Philippines and a few other exceptions, pride themselves on their equidistance,” Piasentini said.
The Philippines signed the Pax Silica declaration in April 2026. With this are plans to establish the Pax Silica Economic Security Zone at the Luzon Economic Corridor.

The US Department of State said that this will be a staging point for the hub and industrial activities. Initial reports said that the project included the processing of critical minerals to make components of high-tech AI conductors,

However, many have decried the Pax Silica initiative, fearing possible displacement of local indigenous people. Many have also feared the possible impacts that the initiative could have on the environment.

While the government has reassured that Pax Silica will have minimal negative effects to the local community and the environment, it did not dissuade hundreds of protesters from questioning who will truly benefit from the AI hub at the end of the day.
Piasentini urged the government to ensure that the process remained transparent.

“The administration must insist on having as much as possible, a process, ensuring as much as possible, a process of implementation and negotiation that is transparent and inclusive, even I would say, at the cost of sacrificing expediency and urgency,” Piasentini said. —Jean Mangaluz/LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Cancer patients at NHS trust harmed by years of unnecessary chemotherapy, report finds
articles.summary:
Trust apologises after findings on treatment of 20 brain tumour patients under oncologist who retired in 2023

Cancer patients were severely harmed after being given years of unnecessary…
articles.byline: Tobi Thomas Health and inequalities correspondent

blocks.text: Cancer patients were severely harmed after being given years of unnecessary chemotherapy treatment by an NHS trust, a report has found.

Some people were misdiagnosed and given inappropriate courses of treatment, while others were incorrectly told that if they stopped chemotherapy they would die, according to a Royal College of Physicians (RCP) report.

The report on the treatment of brain tumour patients at University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire NHS trust was commissioned after concerns were raised by colleagues of Prof Ian Brown, a clinical oncologist, whose patients were handed over after his retirement in 2023.

They found that his patients were on long-term repeated cycles of the chemotherapy drug temozolomide (TMZ), which is far longer than the usual course of treatment, without evidence that continuing it would benefit them. Some of his patients had been left on treatment despite their cancer progressing, when moving to supportive care for their symptoms would have been a better choice.
The report examined the cases of 20 patients. Fifteen of these were found to have received unsatisfactory care and five cases were graded as requiring improvement.

One patient had more than 10 years of chemotherapy and was told they had deadly glioblastoma, according to the report. This was later found to be a grade-1 pilocytic astrocytoma, a low-grade tumour with potentially normal life expectancy that does not require chemotherapy.
Another patient had chemotherapy treatment for a decade and experienced “significant toxicity”, including fatigue, nausea, severe shingles requiring hospital admission, and nausea and vomiting.
Leaders at the trust have apologised for the failures. The legal firm Brabners, which is representing more than 40 patients, is calling for an independent public inquiry.
The report says the trust should ensure that all living patients treated with more than 12 cycles of TMZ have had their case independently reviewed.
Becky Jones received more than 100 cycles of chemotherapy over a 10-year period after she was incorrectly diagnosed with a grade-4 glioblastoma and told she had between six and 12 months to live.
“For years, I questioned why I was still being given chemotherapy when my scans were stable, but I was repeatedly told that without it I would die,” Jones said.
after newsletter promotion

She said seeing the report independently confirm the serious failings that had occurred was “validating” but it was “incredibly painful” to see how many opportunities there had been for the patients’ care to be reviewed. “I now need a full and honest explanation of what happened to me,” Jones said.

Prof Andy Hardy, the trust’s chief executive, and Sue Noyes, its chair, said they were “deeply sorry to all the patients and families affected by failures within our neuro-oncology service under the care of retired clinical oncologist Ian Brown”.

They said: “We recognise the concern, distress and loss of trust experienced by those who placed their faith in us during some of the most difficult moments of their lives. While an apology alone cannot undo the issues experienced, we are clear that meaningful action is being taken.

“These findings make for extremely difficult reading and raise serious questions about individual clinical decisions and historical governance. We will learn from this openly, transparently and with the utmost urgency.

articles.title: North Korea expanded uranium enrichment plant, says IAEA head
articles.summary: IAEA chief Rafael Grossi has said the ongoing expansion of North Korea's uranium enrichment program remains "a cause for serious concern."

image.caption: North Korean state media published pictures of Kim Jong Un at a ski resort as Donald Trump hinted at a possible meeting with himImage: KCNA/REUTERS

blocks.text: United Nations (UN) nuclear watchdog chief Rafael Grossi said on Wednesday North Korea has built an extension on its original uranium-enrichment plant at the Yongbyon nuclear complex.

The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) has been unable to access North Korea since Pyongyang expelled its inspectors in 2009. It now relies primarily on satellite imagery to monitor the country's nuclear activity.
Grossi addressed the ongoing operation of enrichment facilities at Yongbyon and Kangson during a quarterly meeting of the IAEA's Board of Governors.
Kangson lies just southwest of Pyongyang, while the much larger Yongbyon facility is located farther north of the capital.

"Since ​mid-September 2026, a further extension to the original ​Yongbyon enrichment facility has been under construction with the new extension externally complete by ​late October 2026," Grossi said, with no further details.
He said the ongoing expansion of North Korea's uranium enrichment program remains "a cause for serious concern."
Enriched uranium is used as fuel for nuclear power plants and the nuclear reactors that run naval ships and submarines. It can also be used in nuclear weapons.
US President Donald Trump floated the possibility of a meeting with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un as he went to China to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Meanwhile, North Korean state media — which typically operates behind the global news cycle — has only released images of Kim visiting a ski resort and Mount Paektu, making no mention of possible Shenzhen travel plans.
Building a nuclear force
Kim has said he aims to arm the nation with an expansive nuclear force to counter the US and South Korea.
In March, soon after the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran, Kim accused Washington of "global terrorism and aggression."
The Iran war reinforced North Korea's long-standing view that it needs a nuclear arsenal to be able to defend itself against what it sees as its two largest enemies, South Korea and the US.

blocks.caption: North Korean state media published pictures in June showing Kim inspecting a nuclear material production facilityImage: KCNA/KNS/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: North Korea has been subject to various international sanctions over its nuclear weapons development and use of ballistic missile technology. But Pyongyang has repeatedly flouted the restrictions.
In September 2024, North Korea revealed its first covert uranium-enrichment plant. Kim delivered a speech then, including a call for "exponentially" expanding the country's nuclear arsenal.
In April, Grossi told reporters that his agency had confirmed "a rapid increase” in activities at nuclear facilities in North Korea.
In September, the IAEA passed resolutions at its annual conference regarding concerns about the North Korean nuclear program.
Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of Kim Jong Un, said in response that the country's nuclear-armed status was "absolute."
She called those expecting denuclearisation "idiots."
What lessons is North Korea learning from the Iran war?

articles.title: Cadet captain says he's paralyzed from waist down after attack while distributing Remembrance Day poppies

image.caption: Cadet leader Kenneth Kunkel was supervising the distribution of Remembrance Day poppies at the Centre on Barton mall when two boys approached them and blew a loud air horn in the ears of young cadets he was with, police said in a release. (Gofundme)

blocks.text: Hamilton
A cadet leader who underwent spinal surgery after a violent attack says he is currently paralyzed from the waist down and will require months of physical rehabilitation.
Police said Kunkel was attacked Nov. 8 inside a Mandarin restaurant
A cadet leader who underwent spinal surgery after a violent attack says he is paralyzed from the waist down and will require months of physical rehabilitation.
Capt. Kenneth Kunkel provided an update on his situation last week in a statement shared online by a Hamilton member of Parliament.
Kunkel says he is in continual pain and his doctors cannot give him a prognosis at this time, but he remains "hopeful and positive."
He thanked those who have reached out to express support or donated to an online fundraiser set up for his family.
Police have said the Nov. 8 attack stemmed from a confrontation over the harassment of young cadets selling Remembrance Day poppies.
They said two boys approached young air cadets who were selling poppies in front of a restaurant on Barton Street East and blew an air horn "directly into their ears."
Investigators said a man who was supervising the cadets followed the youths into the restaurant to confront them, leading to a struggle.
They allege a woman jumped in to help the youths and assaulted the air cadet leader, who fell to the ground. One of the boys allegedly hit the man multiple times.
A 12-year-old boy and a 48-year-old woman were charged with aggravated assault in the incident.
Kunkel said the youth 'tried to run away'
In his statement, Kunkel said he wanted to clarify some details of what happened that day.

He said he confronted a youth in the restaurant about assaulting one of the cadets and told him they needed to go to the front and call police. The youth "immediately tried to run away," Kunkel said, adding he grabbed the youth's backpack and started walking toward the front of the restaurant while asking staff to call police.
The youth started punching him, he said, and a woman intervened on the youth's behalf. Kunkel said he told her the boy had assaulted a cadet and they needed to speak with police.

While his attention was on the woman, the boy grabbed the lanyard holding Kunkel's car key and ripped it off his neck, he said. When Kunkel reached to grab it back, the woman "blindsided" him, slamming him into a concrete pillar, he said.
"My legs buckled beneath me and I collapsed," he said. "While I was lying on the ground helpless, the young male proceeded to violently punch me directly in the face numerous times."
Kunkel was taken to hospital and underwent surgery that night, he said.
A GoFundMe page set up on behalf of Kunkel and his family said he is the commanding officer of 826 Gryphon Squadron Royal Canadian Air Cadets, and has been with the cadets for 20 years.

articles.title: 'Coalition of the Willing' meets in Berlin: In an era of waning support, Europe remains committed to Ukraine
articles.summary: The "Coalition of the Willing" supporting Ukraine is gathering in Berlin. One of the key issues under discussion is whether Europe will be able to play a role in future negotiations over the…

image.caption: The 'Coalition of the Willing' comprises European countries and EU and NATO leadersImage: Ukrainian Presidential Press Service/Sven Simon/picture alliance

blocks.text: Once again, Berlin is rolling out the red carpet, and once again the focus is on Ukraine: around 20 heads of state and government, primarily from across Europe, are set to gather in the German capital on Thursday (November 19). They will discuss the future of the Eastern European country that has been under attack from Russia since February 2022 and is now facing yet another harsh winter.

Extensive security measures have already been announced for Berlin's government district, pointing to the presence of high-ranking participants. It remains unclear whether Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy will be among them. What does appear certain, however, is the attendance of chief US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, according to several media outlets.

The "Coalition of the Willing" is a group of 36 countries determined not to be deterred from supporting the nation under attack. Unlike other international forums, the group is focused not only on how to support Ukraine militarily and financially in the here and now.
DW interview with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz

Led by Germany, France, and the United Kingdom, the coalition is also prepared, in principle, to help monitor a possible ceasefire within Ukraine itself and to contribute to the complex security guarantees the country would then require, should such a scenario come to pass. The effort dates back to March 2025, when the countries involved first met in London. Now they are gathering in Berlin.

But what can the coalition realistically achieve? Stefan Meister of the German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP) is not overly optimistic. In an interview with DW, he said: "The fundamental problem is that Europe has yet to put forward a proposal. There is no plan outlining what security guarantees Europe would offer, what troops it would be prepared to deploy, what measures it could provide to safeguard a ceasefire, or where it would be willing to make compromises."
Merz: 'Germany has a seat at the table'

Nevertheless, the meeting comes at a moment when some observers believe there may finally be movement toward ending the war. During talks in Abu Dhabi in the United Arab Emirates a few days ago, Russia, Ukraine, and the US managed to agree only on a prisoner exchange. It was a modest step forward.
Further talks are planned, and it has been a long time since the prospects appeared as favorable as they do now for Europe to secure a role in future decisions on war and peace in Ukraine.
Western allies boost Ukraine's defenses but clash over deep strikes
It has repeatedly been argued, both by US officials and by those in power in Russia, that Europe does not speak with a single voice.

Unsurprisingly, this has sparked a debate among EU heads of state and government over who, exactly, could represent Europe in such talks. Could it be German Chancellor Friedrich Merz of the center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU)? After the EU summit in Dublin, Ireland, on Friday, he said: "For the first time, concrete peace talks are expected to take place in the coming weeks with Europe represented. Germany has a seat at the table, that is absolutely clear."
Europe has yet to speak with one voice

But what exactly did that mean? That Germany alone would speak for all of Europe? Hardly. As was also made clear in Berlin on Monday, Europe would be represented by the E3 countries, namely Germany, France, and the non-EU member United Kingdom, joined by Poland and Italy. Official EU representatives, including European Council President António Costa, would also take part.

Stefan Meister of the DGAP believes the debate says a great deal about the pressures Europe itself is under: "Europe's positioning has more to do with domestic political considerations than with developments in the negotiations. Everyone needs to show that they are participating in the talks in some way. Elections will be held next year in France and Poland, and it is still unclear whether French support for Ukraine will continue in its current form after that."

German Deputy Government Spokesperson Sebastian Hille, meanwhile, sought to downplay the debate on Monday over a possible role for Friedrich Merz as chief negotiator. At the federal government's regular press briefing, he said: "This is not about discussing individuals. What matters is that Putin finally understands that he must come to the negotiating table so that we have a chance of achieving peace in the first place."
Can Germany make Europe pay more for Ukraine?
German government spokesperson: Europe now needs stamina

US negotiator Jared Kushner, the son-in-law of President Donald Trump, struck a rather different tone last week. Speaking in Abu Dhabi, he said: "If Europe could identify one person to speak on their behalf, that would be a bigger achievement than getting the Russians to include them in the negotiations."

Government spokesperson Hille responded on Monday: "Europe's strength lies precisely in the unity and cohesion of many countries. We should not allow ourselves to be drawn into debates that others want to frame around this question." Hille emphasized that the situation remained unchanged: peace in Ukraine could only be achieved step by step. Europe, too, would need stamina, perseverance, and a willingness to undertake the painstaking work required to bring it about.
Declining support for Ukraine in German polls

European supporters of Ukraine are also under pressure as public opinion on the issue is shifting, including in Germany. While a broad majority favored helping defend the country in the immediate aftermath of Russia's invasion in the spring of 2022, support has since fallen markedly.

According to the latest ARD DeutschlandTrend survey on the issue, conducted in September 2026, 52% of eligible voters still support weapons deliveries to Ukraine, while 42% believe such support has gone too far. That is the highest level of opposition recorded since the start of the war.

A further study conducted for public broadcaster WDR in November 2026 found that support for Ukraine has become a more polarizing issue in Germany than immigration. According to the survey, 54% of respondents favor continued support for Ukraine, while just under 29% would prefer a rapprochement with Russia, despite its war of aggression against Ukraine.
This article was originally written in German.
